title: Cedar Creek harvest summaries require recorded gains but permit static communities with 19–23% missed presence
abstract: We tested whether plant richness loss requires cumulative local exclusion. We used taxon totals and subplot richness from a Cedar Creek warming and drought experiment in 2017–2022. An integer model gives sharp bounds on binary histories that match both sets of totals. Across 36 subplots, the records require at least 148 gains and 191 losses, despite a net loss of 43 occurrences. Subplot richness raises the minimum gains by 16 beyond taxon totals alone. Yet static true communities fit every summary if sampling misses at least 19.0–23.1% of true presences by treatment, with no false positives and freely placed misses. These are conditional bounds, not estimated error rates. Annual harvest strips moved within subplots. Necessary record exchange thus does not establish colonisation, death or a share of the thermal-tracking gap. All 20 empirical endpoints have zero solver gap and checked witnesses. Exhaustive small-panel enumeration confirms 60 endpoints. Code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and retrieval instructions support reproduction. Source records and possible histories stay external.

display.caption: Recorded richness, sharp gain bounds, and the minimum missed-presence fraction that permits static true communities. Gain ranges are endpoint bounds, not confidence intervals. Black marks use taxon totals only. Harvest strips moved each year.

citations.reason: Weak thermal tracking motivates a test of whether annual records identify occupancy processes. No network summaries are reused.
